chapters.html:
Chapter Notes

I'm guessing there will only be about five or so more chapters after this, but don't quote me on that.

Phainon wakes first, which surprises him for some reason or another. He'd expected Mydei to be an early riser or a light sleeper, but even as Phainon stretches and shoves the blankets off, he doesn't stir. Just sleeps, his bare back to Phainon, side rising and falling. He's... built quite nicely. Muscled and scarless. Warm all over.

Phainon lingers a little longer, tracing the red lines of Mydei's tattoos with his eyes, getting this too strong impulse to touch the place where they converge in the dip of his spine. To press his mouth against Mydei’s shoulder and work his way down. My husband, he thinks, studying the way Mydei’s hair covers the nape of his neck. It shouldn’t mean much, not when they’re arranged as they are, but… Equal, he thinks. That clipped Kremnoan word on Mydei’s tongue. Mine.

Heat floods south. He forces himself to get up, still a mess from last night, desperately needing to wash.

He bathes in near scalding water, scrubbing until his skin is raw and pink, improper things swirling in his head the whole while. Mydei, the feel of him. Rigid muscle and smoother than expected skin, the roughness of his voice, the near softness of his hair tangled in Phainon's fingers. The heat of his mouth, the press of his teeth, the firm lock of his legs around Phainon’s hips. His breath, his grip, his tongue on the shell of Phainon’s ear.

Phainon hides his face in his hands and curses once, softly. He wraps a hand around himself and feels filthy enough to make himself stop. He curses a second time, with feeling, and gets out of the bath.

When he's dry and clothed, he slips back into the bedroom. Mydei is still asleep, light spilling over his shoulder onto the sheets. Phainon looks at him and breathes, awed and almost afraid. The bone at the base of his neck, the dip of his waist, the slight protrusion of his shoulder blades. Maybe he feels Phainon's gaze on him, because he turns onto his back and mumbles something under his breath, one eye cracking open to squint at Phainon. He’s… Titans, is he beautiful. This isn’t what Phainon meant when he said he wanted to take a risk.

"Good morning," he says, a bubble in his throat. His voice comes out all weird. Mydei reaches up to scratch at his chest, grumbling and shutting his eyes again. On his finger, Aglaea's string glows entirely gold.

△

Festivities the day after are much more relaxed. There's music, but they aren't expected to dance until their feet fall off. The streets are still lively and decorated, but Phainon doesn't get swept up as much. He's still congratulated and pulled along for free gifts of bread and sweets and fruits, but it's more like a particularly booming market day than anything else. Phainon squints in the sun and waves at acquaintances and strangers alike, blushing at the occasional catcall. When he reaches Marmoreal Palace, he finds it bustling. Servants running back and forth carrying bundles and dragging carts of supplies. People talking, soldiers preparing. Phainon takes a breath and looks around for Aglaea.

He finds her in the courtyard, supervising a group of men running through sword forms as she talks with Castorice. He clears his throat as he approaches. Both turn to look at him, and something about the weight of their gazes unsettles him. They don't usually look at him like this. He glances down and finds his clothes in order, a hand coming up to rub at his neck, uncertain. Between the straps of his choker, he comes across a tender spot. A bruise, most likely, left by Mydei’s teeth. Heat floods his face as he pushes the straps together in a futile attempt to hide it.

"Phainon," Aglaea greets him. Castorice gives a small bow.

"Lady Aglaea, Lady Castorice," Phainon says, swallowing. "Hello."

Aglaea averts her gaze from his neck. "Aren't you going to join the festivities?" she asks. "There were dancers in Marmoreal Market earlier, they put on quite a lovely performance."

"I'm sure," Phainon says. "Listen, um. About Kremnos—"

"We're sending our forces tomorrow," Aglaea says. "Three thousand men at our disposal, alongside the Kremnoans. I imagine that should be enough. Do you have any concerns?”

A breath. “No,” Phainon says. “No, I just… wondered if you’re coming with us.” Aglaea is far more powerful than the designation of her coreflame might suggest. Romance isn’t the soft thing it sounds like. In Aglaea’s hands, it can be wielded for blood. That, and Phainon has never really been in charge before.

Aglaea smiles, one part regretful and one part apologetic. “I am not,” she says. “I can’t afford to leave Okhema to the jurisdiction of the Council of Elders alone.” Her threads hum softly, and she turns to Castorice, who stands like she feels she should no longer be here. “I’m sending Castorice with you. With her help and that of your newfound husband, I have utmost faith that you will return home victorious.”

“I appreciate your confidence,” Phainon breathes. He’s been a Chrysos Heir for a long time. The perfect vessel for divinity. A prospective hero. But all this time, all throughout the flame chase so far, he feels as though he’s done nothing at all. Just worn this prophecy over his head, waiting for it to pass and garnering attention he’s never felt he deserves.

Phainon of Aedes Elysiae. Bearer of the Strife coreflame. It doesn’t feel right, but perhaps it’s the push he needs, the proof he needs. The strings hum louder.

Aglaea sets a hand on his forearm and says, “I trust you, Phainon. You would do well to trust yourself. I think you’ll find that you won’t need me there at all.”

△

They travel to Castrum Kremnos via dromas. It's a long, slow ride. Phainon doesn't bring much, just a bag of clothes and equipment. Armor he hasn't worn in a long time and his sword, freshly cared for and sharpened by Chartonus.

The day they leave is a warm one, Kephale's sun bearing down on them, making him squint, making him sweat. There's nothing to help by way of a breeze, and Phainon doesn't even have the relief of getting to complain to someone else. He's alone on his dromas, leaning back with an arm over his face to block out the sun. He peeks out from under his wrist, finding Mydei riding beside him, too far to talk without raising his voice, but close enough to look at.

He doesn't look as disgruntled and miserable as Phainon presumably does. He's sitting straight, dressed in his golds and reds with too much skin showing, looking every bit a prince off to war. His face is expressionless and strong, red lining his eyes, hair pulled half back.

He looks regal, wears it the way Phainon wears his coat, with an intrinsic, inherent ease. He’s had little opportunity to grow up as a prince, Phainon knows, but he is one. A king in everything but name. He’s… Titans, why is Phainon the one married to him? Why not someone better equipped to stand at his side?

And yet his hair is still braided by Phainon's hand. One step back from soft. He’d asked Phainon to redo it this morning, stating tradition, grumbling something about equals and refusing to look at Phainon while he did it. The tips of his ears had been red. 

Phainon remembers what the strands felt like between his fingers. The inherently Kremnoan significance of Mydei asking Phainon to do such a thing. The look of him, the feel of him, the roughness of his voice. And now Phainon is thinking about things he ought not to on the back of a dromas, in the company of thousands of marching soldiers. Mydei catches him looking and raises a brow. Phainon has the unfortunate memory of what it's like to kiss him. He lifts a hand and smiles. Mydei makes a rude gesture back, so he clasps a hand to his chest and pretends he's been stabbed. Mydei doesn't laugh, but his lips quirk.

The rest of the ride is slow and uneventful. They stop for lunch halfway, searching for shaded spots along the path to eat meat and cheese sandwiches. Grapes after, as a treat. And then they're back on the road in time to arrive before nightfall. Phainon watches the scenery for a while, makes faces at Mydei for a while, and then gives up and falls asleep. When he wakes, it's to a pebble in the face.

He jolts upright, rubbing the spot and turning to the source. Mydei, with an unimpressed stare on the next dromas over. He taps the corner of his mouth. Phainon wipes a spot of drool in the same spot and curls his lip at him. Mydei taps his head next, where it seems a chunk of Phainon's hair has chosen to stand on end. He smooths it down, then checks his clothes with mild embarrassment. He can hear Mydei laugh at this, a faint, wheezing thing, and he looks up to scowl. Mydei only points ahead.

A mile or two away is Castrum Kremnos, standing in all its golden glory. From here, at least, it doesn't look like a crumbling, war stricken country. The black tide hasn't taken the gates, and they're as resplendent as ever. Mydei's kingdom, Mydei's people. It dawns on Phainon that now they're his people too.

Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, Prince Consort of Castrum Kremnos, to be bearer of the Strife coreflame. Kephale above, that sounds strange.

He looks at Mydei again. Red and gold. Husband, equal. Aglaea’s thread on his finger.

Crowds have gathered outside the gate, and as they get closer, their cheers are deafening. Swords clatter on shields, people shout. They chant the Kremnoan words for Nikador's virtues, Phainon recognizes them from his contests with Mydei and his warriors. A send off to battle or a homecoming. To these people, the sound of hope. Something bubbles up in Phainon's stomach. He's almost nervous. He knows what he is to these people, and while he has no doubt about his ability to do what needs to be done, to save those who need to be saved, it still makes him feel a little bit shaky to think about.

As they approach the city, Phainon makes himself sit tall, ignoring the stiffness in his body from the long ride. He smooths his hair down once more and tries to look like someone these people can trust. Someone worthy of standing beside their crown prince. They ride into the city unimpeded. Phainon waves to the people that catch his eye and feels this deeply.

You're going to be a hero, he thinks. It comes in a soft, feminine voice. I always knew you would be.

He dismounts, smoothing out his robes and coming to stand before the crowd inside the gates. Mydei comes up beside him, shoulder to shoulder, and lifts a hand. With that easy command, the people go quiet. Weary, weathered faces. Men and women in armor, children holding swords too big for their bodies. Tired, fighting people. Phainon commits their faces to memory and swears to himself that he won't let them down.

He listens as Mydei delivers a speech in Kremnoan. The words are sharp on his tongue, but they sound right coming from him. It isn't a beautiful language, not in the way the words are formed or the sounds used to create them, but in the way he speaks it. Like a commander, like a king. Phainon doesn't understand a word he says, but he listens raptly regardless, half certain there are stars in his eyes.

And then Mydei grabs his hand and lifts it skyward, saying something even stronger. Equal , he says, mine . The city erupts in cheers, and all Phainon can do is stare.

△

The battlefield makes Phainon's blood sing louder than it should, run hotter than it should. There's too much energy in his muscles. His sword feels too light; swinging it is almost satisfying but not quite. He carves through titankin like air, and with each body that falls his bloodlust grows. It's maddening, a feeling like an itch, pressure he can't soothe unless he cuts and breaks and destroys, but even that isn't enough. He grits his teeth and thrusts his sword and hisses as his foot gets stuck on a corpse.

Nikador's war cries drown out everything. Phainon has pressed further than the rest of the army has. They've long since left their soldiers behind. The pressure is enough to drive a man mad. He’s afraid he won't be able to stop when the battle is over.

Focus , he thinks. There are so many of them. Beside him, Mydei tears a head from shoulders, splattering himself with gold. He's almost crazed, the same as Phainon is, so much power in his furious hands. Titankin fall by the dozens. Nikador grows louder and louder until Phainon's head is throbbing and his vision tunnels. He thinks he's shouting. He sweeps his sword until his arms scream; but the pain only makes him angrier and angrier and—

There's nothing left to cut down. He stands in a sea of dead titankin, soaked in golden blood, shaking with the fury that flows through him with no outlet. Focus , he thinks. His hands slip on the hilt of his sword. It falls out of his grasp. He's trembling with tension. He needs—

A gauntleted fist to the face, a spiked, armored knee slamming into his side. His vision blurs, refocuses on Mydei, hair matted with blood, eyes blazing. Nikador's voice in his head. Mydei's hands on his shoulders, trying to pull him down, to slam his head into the hard plate on his thigh. Phainon crosses his forearms between Mydei’s to block the blow, gritting his teeth, seeing red.

"Fight back," Mydei growls, and he sounds furious and terrified at once. "I can't—"

Phainon doesn’t wait for him to finish talking. He slams his head into Mydei's chin and pinches the soft part on the inside of his elbow to make him let go, winding up a punch that connects hard with flesh, the impact climbing his arm into his teeth. The feedback scratches that itch, gives him the relief felling the titankin had not.

Mydei grunts and clips him in the shoulder. A second blow is blocked by his wrist. His gauntlets scrape and draw blood. There's so much of it, covering them both. Phainon’s fingers slip in it when he grabs the bare skin above Mydei’s gauntlet, smearing, leaving prints. He pushes Mydei back, making him stumble on a corpse, using the opening to kick him in the waist.

Mydei grunts and twists, recovering swiftly and coming at Phainon’s flank. He grips one of his own wrists and elbows Phainon in the jaw, making him bite his tongue and recoil. Stars dance in his vision. Blood roars in his ears and tastes metallic in his mouth. It takes a moment for his sight to clear. A few more hits. The pain makes his head start to clear too.

"Don't listen," he grits, reaching out. Mydei catches his wrists, pushing him away before he wrenches free. "It's Nikador, Mydei, don't—" He steps wrong on a titankin's hand and stumbles, snagging Mydei by the robes as he topples. He hits the ground hard, knocking the breath from him, making his head spin and those stars come back.

"I can't," Mydei is saying, and he's shaking against Phainon, hands clenched into fists, teeth gritted. He looks scared. Kephale above, he's scared of himself. Phainon is shaking too. He covers Mydei's ears with his hands and pulls him down against his chest, fingers snagging in bloodsoaked hair, pressing hard enough to drown out the noise.

"Don't listen," he says again, pushing Mydei's face against him. The spikes on Mydei's knee armor dig painfully into his inner thigh. The war cries don't stop; his hands shake with the urge to crush, the effort not to. Mydei struggles weakly against him. Teeth sink into his collarbone, but he doesn't budge, keeping his hands where they are. Just curses, just waits this out, tense and straining, head throbbing, violent energy flooding him. Mydei is too heavy against him, too hot, his hair in Phainon’s face, his teeth in Phainon’s clavicle, his armor near to drawing blood. Phainon can hardly breathe.

And then Mydei's hands creep to Phainon's ears too, covering them, the metal of his gauntlets almost painful. Just that, and his focus starts to come back. He breathes raggedly. Mydei's jaw releases, and his brow presses into Phainon's neck.

"Titans," Phainon pants. He stares at the sky, the too darkness of it. The top of Mydei's head, his tangled hair, gold all over. Their position hurts, but Phainon doesn't move, doesn't know if he can, crushed under this weight, exhausted as the bloodlust leaves him. He sweats in his coat. Mydei is hot as a furnace. His breath is damp. Phainon's collar bone aches with the imprints of his teeth. It's still hard to breathe. "We need ear plugs."

Mydei can't hear him, he knows that. He stays in place long enough to catch his breath, then nudges Mydei in the side with his knee. Slowly, he stirs, pushing himself up on his forearms. His hands fall away from Phainon's ears, the sound of the war cries coming back. He's too tired now, though, for them to do anything more than give him a pounding headache. Mydei is covered in blood and dirt and sweat, streaked with it. He looks just as worn as Phainon feels. His fingers snag and pull on bloodied knots in Mydei's hair as he lets his hands fall away. The pain or the sound earns a wince, and then Mydei is pushing himself up with a hand flat on Phainon's chest, winding him all over again as he stands and covers his own ears.

He studies Phainon on the ground, eyes dark, and jerks his head in the direction they came. It’s a long moment before Phainon drags himself to his feet and follows, pressing the bits of cartilage in front of his ears down with blood slick hands. He knows he must look like a mess. Mydei does, but Mydei wears it with strength and purpose. He looks regal, even like this. AA warrior in every sense of the word. Phainon probably just looks like a beaten, stray dog. He stoops to lift his sword from the carnage.

His head throbs as they walk back, dragging themselves further and further from Nikador's cries, stepping over the bodies of dead titankin until they start to see the bodies of soldiers too. They're the only ones that made it this far. Nikador will be even further, their war cries stronger. Phainon worries they'll go mad.

After a safe distance, he unplugs his ears. When he wets his lips, pain pulling at his tongue, he tastes salt and iron, and spits it out. He'd wipe his face, but there isn't a clean inch of fabric on him. Mydei is the same. It's been a long time since Phainon was on a battlefield like this.

"It won't be safe to bring men here without earplugs," Phainon says. "They'll kill each other, we need... Hand signals, or something. Otherwise we can't command them."

Mydei looks at him but says nothing. He turns away, but Phainon keeps watching him. The muscle that tics in his jaw. The tension in his expression, like he's holding back from saying or doing something. Maybe he's just sick of the war cries like Phainon is, but he seems worried about something.

"Mydei," Phainon says.

"It won’t be safe to bring ordinary soldiers this far at all," Mydei tells him. "I asked for men to save people, not to condemn them all to the madness of Strife."

Phainon grabs his elbow, tacky with drying blood. They stick to each other, and Mydei looks at him again intensely, furiously. "So what, then?" Phainon asks.

"If it had been anyone else,” Mydei starts. "Anyone else back there, I would have ripped them to shreds. I would've had that blood on my hands just because the voice of that titan is too… I am stronger than most. Even with earplugs and hand signals, do you really think—"

Phainon pulls him to a stop, turns so they face each other. Beaten, stray dog against dog. "You can't mean you intend to fight Nikador alone?"

"They can die," Mydei says, looking at each of Phainon's eyes in turn. "I can't. I will not ask the soldiers to go this far. Nikador's presence alone will likely be enough to drive them mad, regardless of the measures we take."

Phainon studies him. His steadfast, protective, vengeful determination. The bloodlust of an army but the compassion of a man. Perhaps these things don't exist in contrast, but because of each other. Maybe Mydei fights so others won't have to. "I'm coming with you."

"You're not."

“And what if you’re the one who goes mad?” Phainon asks, perhaps impassioned more than he should be over this. They’re Mydei’s people, sure. This is Mydei’s fight, but he’s the one who asked for help. He’s the one who dragged Phainon into it, who married him on top of it all; he can’t just shove him away now. “Who’s going to stop you?”

“Deliverer—” 

“You married me,” Phainon cuts him off, staring him down. “You’re stuck with me, whether you like it or not. We fight together.”

Perhaps loyalty like this is unearned. A marriage like theirs is little reason to die for someone. The favor he’s been given by Mydei’s people is shallow and unfounded. He owes them nothing but what’s in their contract, and yet…

Mydei once told Phainon he fights like a dog. Perhaps he’s right.

“Stubborn to a fault,” Mydei says under his breath. “HKS.”

“Only when it matters,” Phainon tells him. They hold each other’s gazes a little longer, and then Phainon lets go, their skin sticking with blood. He resumes walking. Behind him, Mydei catches up, then cuffs him around the head, ignoring Phainon’s disgruntled noise and attempts to shove him off.

He tugs hard on Phainon’s ear before he lets go and says, “Even when it doesn’t.”

△

Castrum Kremnos doesn't have baths like Okhema does. Rather than large communal pools, bath houses are rooms with rows of individual stone basins, frequently emptied and refilled as the water gets dirty. Mydei leads the way when they return, barely stopping to grab a clean set of robes before they're storming down the halls to get to the dimly lit, humid chamber. It smells slightly medicinal from the herbal concoctions soldiers mix into the water to soothe muscle aches and injuries. The waters are not blessed by Phagousa here; Phainon too is given a sachet as he enters, despite the fact that he doesn’t intend to soak so much as simply cleanse himself.

Still, he strips and steps gingerly into the bath he adds it to, bloodied and covered in grit from sweat and dirt. His clothes lay in a filthy, torn heap on the ground. He isn't sure how salvageable they are.

Mydei grunts as he sinks into a neighboring basin, immediately beginning to scrub himself clean. He doesn't say anything. Phainon probably shouldn't watch him, but he can't help thinking.

Nikador's war cries are going to be a bigger problem than they thought. He remembers the look in Mydei's eyes, clouded by bloodlust but afraid of that. The fear in his voice as he asked Phainon to fight back. Anyone else, and Mydei would have ripped them apart. He doesn’t know how close they’d gotten to Nikador at that point, but he can only imagine it’s a dozen times worse right next to the source. Enough to bleed through any kind of ear protection. Enough to drive a man truly and honestly mad.

Mydei notices Phainon looking and narrows his eyes, spreading oil from a bottle on his arms and scraping it off with a stirgil, gathering all the blood and dirt. "What?" he asks.

Phainon purses his lips and focuses on cleaning the blood from beneath his fingernails. "Nothing," he says, and his voice comes out weird. "I just... I don't know. I'm thinking about it."

What happens if Phainon goes mad too? He doesn’t think they’re capable of honestly hurting each other. For all their rivalry, for all their sparring, they would both stop before any real injuries occurred. He’s sure of this, and yet…

"Having second thoughts, Deliverer?"

"Not a chance," Phainon says, trying to sound confident, trying to laugh. "We're in this together, husband of mine. I'm just debating how best to get you on your back if need be."

Mydei rubs his wet hands over his face, loosening the filth there. It runs down his temples in gold-brown rivulets. “Innuendo, like poetry, is not your strong suit.”

“Inn—” Phainon laughs for real this time. “That isn’t what I meant. I don’t… or, well, I do, but…”

Mydei sighs visibly. Phainon trails off and finds his gaze avoided in favor of wall or the floor or the edge of the bath. Mydei doesn't speak for a while. A lump forms in the back of Phainon’s throat. He takes this to be the end of the conversation. Reluctantly, he returns to his own bath, scooting forward so he can lean back and wet his hair.

Finally, Mydei speaks into the silence between them. "I suppose you should know, should the worst come to worst," he says. The drip of water as Phainon squeezes out his hair. It runs brown. "I have a weak point."

Phainon pauses, looks at him. "You... Have a weak point?" he repeats. There's a nick on his forehead. It stings from the drips spilling from his hairline, same as the scrape on his forearm from Mydei’s gauntlet. Mydei still isn't looking. Damp hair clings to the nape of his neck. The metal tip of his braid dangles where he looks down as he scrubs himself clean. Firm muscle in his arms and back. Thick red markings. Phainon should stop looking at him. He reaches for a bottle of soap, spilling some into his palm to wash his hair.

"There's no such thing as true immortality." Mydei clears his throat, a rough sound. "If... If I go mad, you'll need to be able to stop me."

He's... awkward, almost. Phainon's little finger heats. A thin gold string drapes over the edge of each bath, connecting them. It’s gold on Phainon's end too, where it hadn’t been before. For some reason, his heart gives a hard thump. "Kill you, you mean," he breathes.

"If it comes to it."

Phainon rubs the soap into his scalp, collecting grit beneath his fingernails. He wets his lips and wonders why it feels like he’s shaking. He clears his throat. “You’d trust me with that?”

A splash. “Are you planning to murder me in my sleep?”

“No,” Phainon says, all airy. He squeezes the suds out of his hair and dunks his head again, running his fingers through the strands. When he comes back up, Mydei shifts in the bath, turning so his back is to Phainon. His hair is filthy; he hasn’t washed it yet. Phainon… wants to do that for him. He doesn’t ask. “Mydei.”

“My tenth thoracic vertebra,” Mydei says, pulling his hair to the side. Somewhere in the dip of his spine, it sits.

“Mydeimos,” Phainon gasps it.

“Remember it well,” Mydei says, and his voice is carefully, artificially level. A pulse of heat through the string between them. Phainon can’t see his face. “I won’t say it again.”

To tell Phainon such a thing. His one vulnerability on an otherwise immortal body. Titans, Phainon doesn’t even know where that is. He’d have to count the knobs of his spine, he’d have to trace his fingers down Mydei’s vertebrae one by one until he finds it, and then he’ll know exactly how he needs to watch Mydei’s back, exactly—

“You’ll strike if need be,” Mydei says, like this is nothing, and Phainon… Phainon doesn’t think he can. It sticks in his throat. It’s like he can feel his heartbeat in their string. He won’t use this knowledge against Mydei. He can’t.

“If need be,” he gets out. “I hope you’ll do the same.”

“I will,” Mydei tells him. It comes out too softly. “So don’t go mad, Deliverer. I’d rather not have to wash your blood from my hair.”

△

Lady Aglaea,

Our first battle in Kremnos has been a success. With our numbers, pushing the titankin back has become far easier for the Kremnoan army. Casualties are low, and we’ve managed to reclaim a dozen neighborhoods. At present, our largest concern is Nikador’s war cries. They amplify and induce bloodlust in those who hear them, and the closer we get, the more they drive the soldiers mad. Earplugs work to an extent, but the soldiers can’t hear, which is a vulnerability.

We aren’t sure if many soldiers will be strong enough to control themselves in Nikador’s presence, so Mydei and I have made the decision to leave the army to battle the titankin while we handle the titan ourselves. Castorice has pledged her help; she is oddly unaffected by the titan’s cries, so she’ll be indispensable in this fight. I have no doubt we’ll reclaim the coreflame soon.

I had another question unrelated to the flame chase, perhaps one that I should have asked in person. When you tied Mydei and myself together with your threads, you mentioned the significance of it turning gold. It has, and I would like to know if I have anything to be concerned about. If you would inform me of the meaning, I would be grateful.

Best,

Phainon

It takes a long time for Mydei’s hair to dry, thick as it is. Hours after his bath, he picks through it with the comb Phainon gifted him. It’s clean but tangled, and the knots don’t want to come undone. An ache forms in his scalp where he rips at them.

He meets his own tired eyes in the mirror. Behind him, seated at the foot of Mydei’s bed—their bed—is Phainon, polishing the knife he keeps at his waist. He’s clean and fluffed up like a dog in the snow. Mydei pulls harder at the comb until he rips this tangle free, tossing a clump of hair on his desk.

“Okay,” Phainon says, standing and setting the knife aside. He’s barefoot and dressed in cottons worn soft and threadbare, chokerless, throat on proud display. Mydei’s mark from their wedding night healing green and brown, stark between the rays of his sun. A cut on his forehead, a scrape on his wrist, bruises speckled here and there. The aftermath of a battle. If he were Kremnoan, Mydei might taste the triumph in each of those marks. But he isn’t, so Mydei keeps those kinds of thoughts to himself.

Phainon comes up behind him and plucks the comb from between his fingers. “I don’t think you can be trusted with this,” he says, picking strands of hair from between the prongs.

Mydei grunts. Seated, his head comes up to Phainon’s chest. They make eye contact in the mirror. “And you can?” he asks, and his voice comes out perfectly level but he curses himself for goading, for wanting Phainon to do this for him. Fingers skim the base of his throat as Phainon collects his hair back.

“Yes,” he answers, and then pauses after that light brush, removing his hands and looking at Mydei through the mirror again. “If that’s okay.”

Please, Mydei thinks. You don’t have to ask. He’s uncomfortable with his own want. It’s easy to want someone carnally, but this is something different. He has no business finding peace in Phainon’s palms. They’re equals in strength, not in weakness. “HKS,” he says, “don’t waste your time.”

He can hear the sound it makes as Phainon’s lips part, see the way his expression softens as he almost frowns. He’s so obvious with his feelings. He holds his heart out in the open for anyone to see, to take, to crush in their fist, to gouge their fingers into. And then he huffs a breath through his nose and says, “I wouldn’t be.”

“Fine, then,” Mydei grunts. Please. Why is he so fragile? Why does he want this from Phainon? The way it felt to not be in control of himself. Anyone else and he would have ripped them apart. But Phainon is strong enough. He’s… Mydei shouldn’t finish that thought. “Suit yourself.”

“I will, then,” Phainon says, pulling all of Mydei’s hair back and beginning to work the comb through the knots. He’s far gentler than Mydei had been, starting at the bottom, holding the knotted sections so they won’t tug at his scalp. His gaze stays turned down, so Mydei has the chance to look at him. He’s softened here, almost painfully so, dressed down and brushing Mydei’s hair. The quiet side of an equal, after the bloodshed is over, when all that’s left is to pick up the pieces and clean the blood from beneath his fingernails.

Strife, Mydei could spit his heart into his palms and find it chewed like a bone tossed to a dog. He could squeeze it in his fist and leave nothing more than pulp. He thinks he can feel Phainon’s body heat behind him, but maybe that’s just his imagination.

“You have beautiful hair,” Phainon tells him. “Like… a lion’s mane, or something.”

Warmth rises to Mydei’s face. “HKS,” he grumbles, but musters little heat. Why does he want so many things? Why could he turn himself inside out with the way his skin aches?

Phainon breathes a laugh. He’s close enough that Mydei can feel it on the crown of his head. “You’ve grown quite fond of calling me that,” he notes. “Was that an inappropriate thing to say?”

He rakes Mydei’s bangs off his forehead, giving him shivers, unaware or unapologetic of the effect he has. He’s always like that. It’s like he doesn’t even know. Mydei is sick with the want and sick of the way Phainon doesn’t seem to notice. “You embarrass us both.”

“I’m not embarrassed, though.” A smile in his voice. Mydei can only see the edge of it in the mirror. He’s beautiful smiling. Mydei could lean back, rest his head against Phainon’s chest to look at him. Maybe Phainon would fold an arm around his shoulders. Maybe he’d brush the rest of the hair away from Mydei’s face and smile again. Fuller, warmer. His body heat fills the gaps between them. Mydei does not move, looking at his hands in his lap, the gold of their string too bright, too warm, pooling in his lap and trailing over his shoulder.

What is this? he wonders. The ache in his chest. The way he can feel each beat of his heart. The way he could close his eyes and just stay for a moment. When did this stop feeling like a cage? Did it ever, really?

“Perhaps you should be,” Mydei replies, because hair is an intimate thing to a Kremnoan, and Phainon knows that, but he still acts clueless.

Phainon pauses to scratch an itch, letting Mydei’s hair fall back into his face, shifting the collar of his shirt a little. Mydei blinks strands out of his eyes and notices the imprints of his teeth purpled around Phainon’s clavicle. “Did you pause to consider that maybe you just need to learn to take a compliment?” Phainon asks. “Why would it be embarrassing that I like your hair? It’s nice hair.”

He likes it, Mydei thinks, and feels like some starved, beaten creature. Begging for scraps, holding on tight enough to bruise. Healing green and brown from Mydei’s mouth, purple from his teeth. Phainon’s fingertips on the shells of his ears, the prongs of the comb against his scalp. Mine, Mydei thinks. Husband, equal, match bound by thread. What’s wrong with him? He’s tired from the battle, still sore from his injuries, that has to be it. He’ll stop feeling this way in the morning.

“Shut up.”

Phainon laughs. He’s still smiling, Mydei can hear that, can practically feel the way it shapes his voice. “Somehow, when you say something like that, I get the inexplicable urge to do the exact opposite.”

Through gritted, self-restraining teeth, “HKS.”

Phainon’s fingers curl over Mydei’s bare shoulder as he leans forward to swap the comb for the metal cuff Mydei uses to secure the braid in his hair. His abdomen against Mydei’s back, his chest against the back of Mydei’s head. “I still think that’s a pet name,” he says, and doesn’t step away. “At least the way you use it.”

“Would you keep a hyena as a pet?” The backs of Phainon’s fingers skim the underside of his chin. He’s too close, all living heat and the smell of pine resin. He gathers the section of hair behind Mydei’s ear to braid it upside down, his arms a cage around Mydei’s head. It would be so easy to bite him again, to tilt his face down and sink his teeth into Phainon’s forearm. He wants to, wants to do something. His skin itches with Phainon so close.

“Is that what it means?” Phainon chuckles. He fumbles horribly, braiding like this. Mydei doesn’t know why he stays still, other than the way his heart roars in his ears. “Well… They’re a little bit cute, aren’t they?” A pause. “Did you know they give birth through their penises?”

“What?” Mydei tips his head back to glower at him.

Phainon’s laughter shakes him. “The females have a fake one that they give birth through. It sounds very painful, actually. A senior at the Grove told me.” He loses his hold of one of the sections of the braid, the strands tangling together and becoming unsalvageable. Mydei shoves him off and undoes it with his fingers, scowling.

“You’re a fool,” he says, but finds his incredulity shifting into laughter. Phainon laughs too, an easy, wheezing, unfairly contagious thing. Mydei has it memorized, has for weeks, and that’s… He doesn’t know. He rubs his fingers into his forehead and finds the laugh stilling in his throat. He braids his hair and turns to pull the cuff from Phainon’s loose fingers, putting them face to face. He has to look up to meet Phainon’s eyes. They’re both silent, and Phainon’s smile shifts into something softer. The fluff of his hair. He doesn’t wear Mydei’s braid anymore. It would be strange to ask him to, when the tradition doesn’t belong to him. His hair is far too short for it anyway.

He watches Phainon’s gaze fall to his mouth, feels the brush of fingertips on the outside of one parted knee. Phainon fits between them, more than close enough to touch. “Hey…”

“Do it, Deliverer,” Mydei says, tilting his head up like a challenge, and Phainon bends to kiss him.

It’s gentler than he meant it to be, just a press of lips and not teeth and tongue. Phainon’s tentative hand on the back of his neck, fingers slipping into his hair. His eyes are closed. His inhale is soft through his nose, softer through his mouth as he exhales when they separate. And then he kisses Mydei again, tilting his head just so, parting his lips, stumbling closer when Mydei tugs him in by a hand fisted in his shirt. He breathes a laugh, fits his free hand on Mydei’s hip, drawing back with half-lidded eyes before he kisses Mydei properly, licking shallowly into his mouth, fingers slipping all the way into his hair.

And yet he’s still too gentle. Mydei is used to the roughness of a spar, the way a bedding is tantamount to a battle, but in this, unlike in everything else, Phainon doesn’t bother with competition. He hadn’t much the first time either, but Mydei had written that off as inexperience. Maybe not. Maybe he’s just—

“Titans, you’re beautiful,” Phainon murmurs against him. “Did I tell you that? You’re a sight to behold at war, and here it’s like—” Mydei tries to shut him up with a kiss, but it only works for so long before Phainon’s hand on his hip slides up his ribs to his chest, pressing him lightly back. “—It’s like I’m the only one who gets to see the aftermath. My husband, my—”

“Don’t,” Mydei says before he can finish that thought, the tip of his nose brushing the side of Phainon’s, parted mouth stretching to his. They kiss, slowly, deeply. Mydei’s fist never loosens in Phainon’s shirt. Phainon holds him by the shoulder, but doesn't stop Mydei from trapping him between his thighs.

“Why can’t I say it?” he asks, too breathy, too wanting when Mydei has hardly touched him at all.

Mydei’s teeth on his lip. “You don’t know what it means.”

“I do,” Phainon protests. His hand is back on Mydei’s leg, sliding up his knee, thumb digging into his inner thigh. “Equal,” he says.

“Don’t,” Mydei grits.

“You called me that,” Phainon says into his mouth. Mydei’s legs part wider, he presses closer, hand winding around Mydei’s back to splay at the center of his spine, fingertips like stars for their heat. “In front of all of your people, you claimed me as that. Why can’t I use it too?”

“You don’t understand it,” Mydei insists, grabbing his arm, the back of his neck. Their foreheads press. Phainon looks at him, his mouth, and back.

“It means you're my equal,” he murmurs, and presses their lips together once, pulls back. “It means you match my strength, my weakness.” Another kiss. Mydei finds himself robbed of breath. “It means we fight together on the battlefield and off it. It means I’ll watch your back, it means I get to see you in the aftermath, to comb your hair and—”

“Shut up.”

Phainon closes his eyes and softens his hold. “I won’t say it again, if you really don’t want me to.”

No, Mydei thinks, and curses himself for it. Say it. Please. “Fool,” he says aloud. Fearing the wrong things. Mydei wants him with a vengeance, would claim him as his equal in front of every soul in Amphoreus if he could.

“Sorry.” Phainon laughs softly.

“It means more than you think it does,” Mydei tells him. “You can’t use it for someone who’s only a lover.”

“Then why,” Phainon starts, palm shifting an inch up Mydei’s back, “would you use it for me? If that’s all I am, if you see me as nothing more than…” He trails off. 

Mydei doesn’t have an answer to that question. Phainon looks at him so intensely, searching each eye in turn, gaze dipping back to his mouth. His hair tickles Mydei’s forehead.

“Mydei,” he breathes. They kiss. He paws at Mydei’s hip.

“Don’t, Deliverer.” He’s too airy; he sounds like he wants it. He does. Titans, he does.

“Equal.” He swallows it up. Phainon presses into him, squeezing his thigh tight enough to bruise, rocking them together and making a low, starved sound. “Did I say it right?”

“HKS.” Mydei crosses his legs behind Phainon, trapping him close, cursing him when a hand winds into his hair and tugs, pulling his head back, making him bare his neck. Phainon’s mouth on his throat. The heat of him, the friction where they meet. He fists one hand in Phainon’s shirt, the other tangling in his hair, silken in his fingers, holding Phainon to him.

“Do you hate it?” Phainon asks, nosing the underside of Mydei’s jaw, breathing him in, kissing his pulse point. He’s unreasonably earnest, the insecurity bleeding into his voice in a way that makes Mydei nauseous. Sick with the thought of him worrying, sick with the words he’ll have to say to reassure him.

“No,” he grits, face hot. He twists his fingers in Phainon’s hair, pulling on it. “Does it seem like I hate it?”

A pained, breathy laugh. One of Phainon’s hands slips between them, fumbling at their waistbands. “So can I—?”

“Can you face the consequences?” Mydei pants, reaching to help him, groaning at the touch of skin on skin. Phainon wraps around them both, face pressed hard into the side of Mydei’s neck.

“Consequences?” He tries to laugh, but he’s too shaky, body tight and trembling. Mydei’s hand folds over his, and Phainon shifts to look down, to watch the way they move together. “Titans,” he breathes, more of a moan than a word.

“The consequences,” Mydei repeats, holding the back of his head, petting through his hair, arching into him, “of calling me your equal.”

“I already married you,” Phainon reminds him. “I’m already in this for life.”

The gold thread tangles between them. “We married to ally our people. You didn’t choose me.”

“Neither did you.”

“And yet,” Mydei says. Equal, he thinks. Do you want this? Are you happy?

Phainon shudders, grips them tight. His breath is hot against Mydei’s neck. “And yet.” He curses softly under his breath, and then there’s silence between them. Just the passage of air and the rhythm of their hands. A little longer; Phainon comes to completion and whispers it. “Equal,” he says. “Titans, Mydei.”

“Do you mean it?” Mydei asks him.

Phainon slumps against his torso, just breathing, heart thundering in his chest hard enough for Mydei to feel. He slides his fingers through Phainon’s hair. Over and over, gentler than he knew himself capable.

“I want to,” Phainon tells him. “I really do, if you’ll let me.”

“Alright.”

Phainon’s hand is sticky and slow. Mydei’s thighs twitch and clamp. He holds Phainon like a vice as he finishes too.

“I don’t know what this is,” Phainon says, trying to clean himself up. “And I’m scared, sure, but why don’t we make the best of it?”

Mydei’s cheek against his hair. He shuts his eyes and breathes. “You’re so sure, suddenly.”

“Because…” Reluctantly, Phainon pulls back. His expression is horribly, painfully open. “Who knows how much time we really have left?”

△

At night, Mydei sleeps with his back to Phainon. Strange how easily they’ve settled into sharing a bed and a space.

Mydei has long been used to sharing tents and fires with the men in the Kremnoan detachment. This isn’t much different than that, he tells himself. Phainon is just another body in proximity, and yet Mydei is aware of him like a troublesome beam of light at bedtime.

The sound of his breath, the shift in the mattress when he moves. The fact that he’s here and he’s warm and he’s a repeated source of Mydei’s pleasure. 

Mydei stays still for a long time, steadying his breathing. Four counts in, four counts out. His eyes open, and he stares at the wall. Sighs, softly. Thinks of blood on his hands.

This is what my world has come to, he thinks. A war he’s only half certain he can win. A husband he can’t wrap his head around. An empty throne and a blood slick spear in his hands. What does he do with the people when this is all over?

The tentative touch of fingers on his back, climbing one shoulder blade, tracing the stark lines of his tattoos. He stiffens, but Phainon still wanders up until he brushes the ends of Mydei’s hair, the knob at the top of his spine.

“What are you doing?”

“One,” Phainon whispers. Down an inch. “Two.”

Shivers. Mydei could quake the earth with them. Phainon’s fingers pass over each of his vertebrae as he counts them with more breath than voice. He stops in the middle of Mydei’s back and murmurs, “ten.” His touch is barely more than air. “It’s here, then?” he asks, and his voice is soft and weary. Sleepless, like Mydei. Worn down by the images of war, the sensations of it in his hands.

Maybe not. Maybe he just happened to stir awake, or maybe other things cause him to struggle with sleep. Mydei doesn’t know him well enough to have knowledge of these things. Not yet. He comes to the realization that he doesn’t really know Phainon at all.

“Yes,” he admits, a lump in his throat from the vulnerability of it. “Stab me there and I will die.”

Phainon’s palm presses flat over the spot. Warmth in his hands. Mydei is hyper aware of it, a psychological sensitivity attuned to that spot. The mattress shifts. Phainon’s brow presses against the nape of his neck as he slides closer. He yawns softly, sniffles, softened by proximity to sleep.

“I’ll guard it,” he whispers. Too warm, too close. There’s nothing to look at but the wall. Mydei’s hand fisted in the sheets. Phainon couldn’t fight off a kitten right now. Perhaps that’s the part that sticks. Equals in weakness, not only in strength. Phainon falls asleep, tucked close and trusting, and Mydei lays awake with a too loud heart trying to beat its way out of his chest.

△

They rally the soldiers over the next two weeks. Mydei’s are long weary, but Phainon's are fresh, and it's contagious. Morale is as high as it's been since Eurypon died. The men are training with hand signals and ear plugs, and they're determined. They're ready to be heroes, every one of them.

The Kremnoans have started calling Mydei king. It gives him an odd, stomach turning sensation. He reminds them that he hasn’t taken the throne, but it does little to quell the flood.

It's hot out; dry, heavy heat. Mydei watches the soldiers train in the palace's courtyard, practicing sword and spear forms. Their breathing is labored, their bodies shine with sweat. Hundreds of them, thousands of men dedicated to fighting this war at his side. Each one has a family and friends to come home to. Each one has only their life to give, and war is cruel in honoring that. Valorous death before glorious return. Many fight with the expectation of dying, with the near want of it. So little do they see the value of a life.

The Maiden of War sits on a stone bench in the courtyard under a scant amount of shade provided by a tree. Her scythe rests at her feet. A needle glints between her fingers as she works on a bundle of fabric in her lap. Her face is downturned. Her hair sways with the breeze.

Mydei approaches, and she looks up. "Lord Mydeimos," she greets, hands pausing their work. It doesn't seem to be clothing. It's bright, colorful felt. Red and blue. Eyes and a thin line for a mouth embroidered into it. A deflated... seal, perhaps. She scrunches it up and folds her hands over it.

Mydei nods to her. "Lady Castorice," he greets back. An odd silence between them. "How do you find Castrum Kremnos?"

"It's a grand city," she answers, meeting his eyes only briefly. She shifts on the bench, seeming to try to put more space between them. Mydei remembers the way she'd flinched upon almost bumping into him, and takes a step back for her comfort. He can't imagine what it would feel like to kill with only a touch. To regard your own skin as monstrous. She sighs as she notices him giving her space. "I apologize," she says.

"Don't," Mydei tells her. "I understand, but if it helps, I can't die."

She smiles slightly, sadly. "I'd rather not take my chances." One of her hands comes down to adjust her shoe, revealing blisters on her heel before she fixes it. She notices Mydei looking and answers his question before he can ask it. "I can't ride the dromases, so I walk."

"I see," Mydei says. She sits on the far edge of the bench. Slowly, he takes a seat on the opposite side, space enough for five between them. He folds his arms and watches the men train, pairs of them sparring. One thrusts his sword, another parries. Castorice returns to her sewing, and Mydei peeks out the corner of his eye to get a better look at it. Unstuffed, the fabric is loose and unshapely, but he can make up what must be a tail, a wider section for the body. A seal indeed. It's... cute. Castorice pricks her finger on the needle and brings it to her mouth.

"Are you prepared to lead them?" Mydei asks her.

"Ah..." Her hand withdraws, gold blood welling at the tip of her index finger. "I'm not much of a leader, but I will try with the help of your officers."

"They respect you."

A sigh or a huffed laugh. "They fear me."

Mydei remembers her on the battlefield. The scythe in her hands, a fitting weapon for the Servant of Death. The way she wields it is graceful, felling titankin without getting so much as a drop of ichor on her skirts. Perhaps she's feared in Okhema, but Mydei can't see his people watching her with anything but admiration. "Not mine," he says. He's caught wind of whispers from his soldiers about her. She doesn't reply.

"Why don't Nikador's cries affect you?" he asks. She hums and rethreads her needle after she has to adjust a stitch.

"I guide the dead and the dying," she says. "I don't want to be the one to create them.”

The war cries amplify bloodlust, not create it. Perhaps Castorice doesn't contain a single seed of Strife to grow. "What will you do when you find Thanatos?" Mydei asks her. "When you assume their divinity?"

"I don't know," she says, shaking her head. "If I can, perhaps I'll rid the world of death."

"Without death, there is no value in life." She stills, and the set of her shoulders is tired. She's seen more bloodshed and death than Mydei can dream of. Studying her now, seeing that in her and the way she's still here to do everything she can to help, he respects her terribly.

"Perhaps," she says faintly. "And what of you? What do you intend to do when Nikador falls?"

When the bloodshed is over, and all that is left are the pieces to stitch back together. The black tide has taken so much from them. Swept land into eternal night that he doesn't know how to get back. Perhaps, after it all, Castrum Kremnos will still be lost. "I only wish to guide my people to something more peaceful," he answers. She seems to understand this.

△

Phainon wears armor today. Silver next to Mydei's gold. Smooth, shining plate on his legs and arms. His breastplate is engraved with a sun to match the one on his throat. The light glints off of him. The daylight gives him a halo as he stands at Mydei's side, a little taller because of his boots, looking every bit a prince's equal. Their men wait, straight backed, standing in neat formations, waiting for orders. They're silent and disciplined, and Mydei looks at the rows and rows of bodies, and swears to himself that they're going to win this. If not for him, for them, for their families. If not for glory, then for the right to rest.

A hand claps his back. Krateros, scarred and weathered, gives him a firm nod. He's lost vision in one eye, but his gaze is strong, and he's the closest to a father Mydei has ever had. "Are you ready, Son of Gorgo?" he asks. "Will you lead us to victory?"

Mydei holds his gaze. Nods once, firmly. "You have my word."

Krateros holds out a hand, and Mydei clasps it. He squeezes hard enough to hurt. "I'm proud of you, boy."

"Save it for when Nikador has fallen," Mydei tells him, not liking the way his throat threatens to choke. Krateros smiles, and for a moment, Mydei feels like a child again, fresh from the River of Souls and lost. Born a prince but not raised one. Wholly unprepared to lead. When this is over, Krateros will ask him to take the throne again, he knows. Mydei will have to disappoint him horribly. But it's in his destiny, isn't it? To lead Castrum Kremnos to its fall. Mydei was never meant to be king.

"After we win, then," Krateros agrees, squeezing a little harder. His gaze falls behind Mydei to Phainon, where he's begun talking to Castorice, confident and gleaming in his armor. He finally lets Mydei's hand go. "I was doubtful, at first," he says, nodding in Phainon's direction. "But you've chosen well.”

"He's..." Mydei looks at him too. Watches him laugh with the sound of it memorized. Watches him smile with the sight of it imprinted on the backs of his eyelids. Watches him take half a step and make himself stumble over nothing. Castorice hops back with her eyes wide and a hand over her mouth. Mydei takes a breath and breathes it out as a tired laugh. "He's a fool," he says, "but there's nothing I can do but be drawn to him."

Krateros lays a hand on his shoulder and laughs too. “Gorgo and Eurypon were the same,” he says. “Equals in everything, yet at odds in everything. You’ve never known anyone who matches you so well, have you?”

Phainon recovers, laughing it off. The sound of it is terribly contagious. Castorice kisses her knuckles as her eyes crinkle, as Mydei’s stomach turns. “No,” he admits. “He’s the only one.”

What an odd coincidence they are. To meet like this, to be bound like this, and still end up equals like they had done it by choice. Maybe in another life, they would have. Maybe in another life, Mydei would have chosen him over anyone else in the world. Despite his foolishness, despite the way he loves to push Mydei’s buttons, despite his titansdamned poetry, Mydei probably would.

“Do you love him, then?”

Krateros speaks in the Kremnoan language; the word he uses for love is a borrowed one. Mydei looks at him, almost startled to hear it. “We don’t have a word for that,” he says.

“No,” Krateros agrees. He gazes at the soldiers, then back at Mydei. “But you call him equal. Many would argue that it’s the same.”

“It’s not,” Mydei protests. Krateros only shrugs and pats his shoulder before letting it drop. Mydei takes a couple of breaths in silence. It prickles at him. Love. Phainon’s palm at the center of his back. “I don’t know what it’s supposed to feel like,” he says.

Krateros smiles. “And I do?” His voice is a gruff, amused thing. “No, I just thought I’d ask.”

Mydei frowns and folds his arms. “Why?”

Krateros doesn’t respond, just gestures vaguely and changes the subject. “They’ve been waiting a long time, lad. Are you ready to bring them victory?”

“Yes,” Mydei says, leaving it alone.

Krateros nods, holding his gaze. Proud of him, perhaps. “Go, then.”

So Mydei takes a breath and nods back. Love, he scoffs, making his way to Phainon. He’s surprised at the touch of Mydei’s hand on his shoulder, eyes wide, mouth parting. Love. It almost makes him angry. Mydei drags him into a kiss, hard and pressing, and shoves him off. “Are you ready, Deliverer?” he asks.

Phainon’s mouth opens, closes. He lets out a soft, stunned uh?, one hand lifting to his mouth before he drops it swiftly. “Yes,” he says. “Yes, I’m— Never been readier. I’m the most ready you’ve ever seen, uh…”

“HKS,” Mydei mutters. Phainon still looks lost. He meets Castorice’s wide gaze over Phainon’s shoulder, and feels his ears heat. He turns away, facing the men waiting to march. “Let’s go then.”

Chapter Notes
